summary: Prohibits unfair or deceptive acts or practices; FTC uses it to enforce reasonable data security and privacy representations.
applies_to: Most for-profit businesses in commerce. Statutory carve-outs in 45(a)(2) include banks, S&Ls, federal credit unions, common carriers subject to the Acts to regulate commerce, and air carriers/foreign air carriers.

citation: 32 CFR Part 170; DFARS 252.204-7021 (48 CFR rule, 90 FR 43560)
summary: Requires CMMC status (Level 1 self; Level 2 self or C3PAO; Level 3 DIBCAC) as a condition of DoD award; Level 2 = NIST SP 800-171 R2, Level 3 adds NIST SP 800-172.
applies_to: DoD contractors and subcontractors that process, store or transmit FCI or CUI on contractor information systems (flows down the supply chain).
size_thresholds: No small-business exemption. Applies to DoD solicitations/contracts above the micro-purchase threshold; excludes procurements exclusively for COTS items (32 CFR 170.3(c)).
status: 32 CFR 170 effective Dec 16, 2024; DFARS acquisition rule effective Nov 10, 2025 = start of Phase 1. Phase 2 begins one year after Phase 1 (Nov 10, 2026), Phase 3 one year later, Phase 4 (full) one year after that. Phase 2 suspended: the DoD (Department of War) CIO memorandum of 2026-07-13 suspended the Phase 2 transition planned for 2026-11-10. Under DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0025, Revision 3 (DFARS 240.371-5), clause 252.204-7021 is used until 2028-11-09 only when a program office requires a specific CMMC level, and from 2028-11-10 whenever contractor systems process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI. During the suspension requiring activities may require Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self); SP 800-171 Rev. 2 under DFARS 252.204-7012 still applies. 32 CFR Part 170 is unchanged.

short_name: DFARS Safeguarding CDI & Cyber Incident Reporting
summary: Implement NIST SP 800-171 on covered contractor systems; report cyber incidents to DoD within 72 hours; preserve images; flow down; cloud providers must meet FedRAMP Moderate equivalent.
applies_to: DoD contractors/subcontractors with covered defense information.

short_name: FAR Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
summary: Basic safeguarding requirements (access control, identification/authentication, media sanitization, physical access, boundary protection, patching, malware protection) for systems holding Federal Contract Information.
applies_to: Federal contractors/subcontractors (any agency) whose systems process FCI.
status: In force (NOV 2021 clause version). FAR overhaul: under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation (adopted by DoD, GSA, DHS, DOE, VA and most other agencies; list read on acquisition.gov 2026-10-08), new solicitations and awards carry FAR 52.240-93, Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems, with the same 15 requirements and flow-down. Contracts awarded earlier keep FAR 52.204-21 until modified.

summary: Prohibits providing or using covered telecommunications/video surveillance equipment or services (e.g., Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, Hytera) in federal contracting; requires reporting if discovered.
applies_to: Federal contractors, including distributors reselling ICT/security products to government.

citation: CBP program; SAFE Port Act of 2006 (voluntary)
summary: Voluntary supply-chain security partnership; members must meet Minimum Security Criteria that include a cybersecurity section plus business-partner due diligence and risk assessment.
applies_to: Importers/exporters, carriers, customs brokers, consolidators, port/terminal operators, foreign manufacturers (by entity type).
status: Active voluntary program; MSC updated (Importers MSC Oct 2021).

citation: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106); Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216, 88 FR 51896)
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management, strategy and governance; Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents.
applies_to: Exchange Act reporting companies (public issuers), including public companies in any sector.
size_thresholds: No exemption by size; smaller reporting companies received a later Item 1.05 compliance date (June 15, 2024 vs. Dec 18, 2023).
status: In force; effective Sept 5, 2023. No rescission found in Federal Register as of 2026-09-25.

short_name: CCPA/CPRA + 2026 CPPA regulations (cyber audits, risk assessments, ADMT)
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100 et seq. (business def. 1798.140(d)); Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7000 et seq. (cyber audits 7120-7124)
summary: Consumer privacy rights, reasonable security; new regs require independent annual cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, and ADMT notices/opt-outs.
applies_to: For-profit businesses doing business in California that meet any threshold.
size_thresholds: Business if ANY of: annual gross revenue > $25,000,000 as CPI-adjusted (= $26,625,000 effective Jan 1, 2025); buys/sells/shares PI of 100,000+ consumers or households; or derives 50%+ of revenue from selling/sharing PI. Cyber audit required if 50%+ revenue from selling/sharing PI, OR revenue threshold met AND processed PI of 250,000+ consumers/households or sensitive PI of 50,000+ consumers. First audit report due Apr 1, 2028 (2026 revenue > $100M), Apr 1, 2029 ($50M-$100M), Apr 1, 2030 (< $50M). Data subject to GLBA is exempt at the data level (Civ. Code 1798.145(e)), except the 1798.150 breach private right of action.
status: Regulations approved by OAL Sept 22, 2025; effective Jan 1, 2026. ADMT compliance for existing uses by Jan 1, 2027. Risk-assessment submissions for 2026-2027 due Apr 1, 2028.
